planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this compact hybrid stays tidy enough for smaller borders and foundation plantings.

directions: This compact French hybrid mock orange bears clusters of single, pure-white flowers up to an inch across, carrying the strong sweet orange-blossom fragrance typical of the group in a much more restrained, upright-rounded frame than older tall selections. Its dense habit and smaller mature size make it a good fit for foundation plantings and mixed borders where larger mock oranges would quickly outgrow the space. Prune immediately after flowering, removing a portion of the oldest canes at the base every couple of years to keep the shrub renewed and encourage strong new flowering wood for the following season. It adapts to a wide range of well-drained soils and tolerates light shade, though flowering is heaviest in full sun.
sources: Hillier Manual of Trees and Shrubs
